newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIAN AGRICULTURAL BANK SAYS NO MORE SOFT LOANS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIAN AGRICULTURAL BANK SAYS NO MORE SOFT LOANS.

text.p: Lithuania's huge state-run Agricultural Bank says that it will no longer issue soft loans the country's troubled farming sector but will carry the burden of past loans until 1999, daily Lietuvos rytas said on Monday.

"The consequences of soft loans issued in the past will be felt for a few more years since the maturity on most has been prolonged until the end of 1999," Vaclovas Litvinas, the bank's chairman, said in an interview to the paper.
He added that as of March 5 this year, the bank no longer had to provide soft loans to agricultural enterprises.
But he said that the bank would continue to serve the agricultural sector and that 60 percent of its loans would still go to the sector.
The bank, which has been slated for privatisation, had a net profit last year of 25.5 million litas.
Litvinas said that the bank's forecast for 1997 is four to five million litas as it plans to invest around 30 million litas in its computer network.
The newspaper also quoted Litvinas as saying that thirteen investors had expressed an interest in participating in the privatisation of the bank.
They include three Lithuanian banks, Vilniaus Bank, Hermis Bank and Snoras Bank, as well as banks from Italy, Spain, Germany and other countries, Litvinas told the newspaper.
